eJ3RzGoQC4s.summary: Adam Curtis' multi-part documentary on how Freud's ideas and Edward Bernays' public relations shaped consumer culture and political control. It argues that business and government learned to manufacture desires.
eJ3RzGoQC4s.why: HN recommends it often and strongly as an eye-opening account of marketing psychology and the engineering of consumer society.

eG0KrT6pBPk.summary: Moxie Marlinspike's DEF CON 18 talk on changing threats to privacy argues that surveillance arrived through convenient services and network effects, so opting out is not a real solution. It also includes his framing of getting social democracy rather than the fascism people feared.
eG0KrT6pBPk.why: Cited repeatedly to rebut 'just don't use Facebook' arguments and to explain why tracking becomes hard to escape at critical mass.

ecIWPzGEbFc.summary: Robert C. Martin (Uncle Bob) traces the history of software from 1948 to today, looking at the problems programmers faced, how they were solved, and what mistakes the profession made. He then projects where the field is going, including professionalism and regulation.
ecIWPzGEbFc.why: HN recommends it as an engaging overview of programming history and an argument for professional standards, citing the agile manifesto section and the claim that software has advanced little since the 1950s.

eviSykqSUUw.summary: Brian Karis's SIGGRAPH 2021 talk explains how Unreal Engine 5's Nanite virtualized geometry works. It covers mesh import, the data structures, streaming, decompression, culling, software and hardware rasterization, and shading.
eviSykqSUUw.why: HN treats it as the definitive deep dive on Nanite, admired for the engineering ambition behind pixel-sized triangles and compute-driven rendering.

eMmNy11Mn7g.summary: People Make Games investigates the unregulated CS:GO skin gambling economy and Valve's role in it. It includes interviews with people who lost large sums and examines why Valve does not intervene.
eMmNy11Mn7g.why: HN recommends it as well-researched reporting on skin gambling, especially its effect on minors, in threads about gambling and Valve.

e3msMuwqp-o.summary: The final lecture of Richard Hamming's Learning to Learn course, from 1995, based on his well-known talk 'You and Your Research'. It covers how to do important work and build a career.
e3msMuwqp-o.why: HN people recommend it as the capstone of Hamming's course and as career advice about working on important problems.

eMlx5fFNoYc.summary: 3Blue1Brown's visual walkthrough of the attention mechanism inside transformers, covering self-attention, multiple heads and cross-attention. It is chapter 6 of his deep learning series.
eMlx5fFNoYc.why: HN treats it as the go-to visual explanation of attention, recommended to people who find text-based transformer explainers hard to follow.

eOti3kKWX-c.summary: CuriousMarc powers up a vintage HP 5061A cesium beam clock and explains both the quantum principle and the HP implementation in detail. It is part of a longer atomic clock series.
eOti3kKWX-c.why: HN calls it one of the best explanations of how atomic clocks actually work.

eqQBubilSXU.summary: A motorcycle safety video on the SMIDSY (sorry mate, I didn't see you) accident, explaining the perception and optical illusion that makes drivers fail to see riders, and how riders can spot the signs and avoid it.
eqQBubilSXU.why: HN considers it an outstanding explanation of why drivers miss motorcycles and cyclists, linked in threads on visibility and junction crashes.

eU5Dn-WaElI.summary: Jim Pavloff rebuilds the Prodigy track Smack My Bitch Up in Ableton, identifying the samples used and recreating the track by hand.
eU5Dn-WaElI.why: Recommended as a fun, in-depth look at how sampling and music production work, and as proof that skilled humans can reconstruct tracks from scratch.

elvOZm0d4H0.summary: Numberphile's James Grime explains Cantor's result that some infinities are bigger than others, including why the reals outnumber the integers. It is a short, accessible introduction to countable and uncountable infinity.
elvOZm0d4H0.why: HN people recommend it as a clear introduction to different sizes of infinity that non-mathematicians can follow.

ez773teNFYA.summary: Lex Fridman interviews Stephen Wolfram for about three hours on cellular automata, computation, the Wolfram Physics Project and his career with Mathematica and Wolfram Alpha.
ez773teNFYA.why: HN points to it as an accessible long-form introduction to Wolfram's ideas and a window into his passion, though some are critical of his claims.

ezVk1ahRF78.summary: Hans Rosling's TEDxSummit talk asks whether some religions have higher birth rates and how that affects population growth. He charts data across time and religions and reaches a surprising conclusion about fertility.
ezVk1ahRF78.why: Recommended whenever population growth comes up, as a data-driven correction to common assumptions.

e7wFotDKEF4.summary: A long video essay arguing that Koko the gorilla probably could not actually use sign language. It examines the cherry-picked data and the lack of transparency behind the claims, drawing on published critiques.
e7wFotDKEF4.why: Recommended as a thorough debunking of Koko's supposed language ability in threads about animal communication.

esQyYGezS7c.summary: Veritasium visits NIST to explain Standard Reference Materials, the carefully characterized items such as peanut butter used to calibrate instruments and keep measurements consistent. It covers why they exist and why they are expensive.
esQyYGezS7c.why: Whenever NIST's pricey peanut butter or reference materials come up, commenters point to this as the clear explanation of why they exist.

e08kOj2kISU.summary: David Schachter describes how he made a data-collection Python program run 114,000 times faster, drawing on decades of experience. The talk covers pipelining, cache effects and other optimization lessons.
e08kOj2kISU.why: A favorite tech talk on HN for showing that hardware knowledge and generalist skills beat simply adding machines.

e3K5UxWRRuY.summary: Joscha Bach's 35C3 talk offers an AI perspective on the soul, covering perception, mental representation, agency, consciousness and selfhood as things that can arise in a computational system like the brain.
e3K5UxWRRuY.why: HN commenters call it lucid and fluff-free, and point to Bach as one of the most interesting voices on AI, consciousness and philosophy.

eC7xzavzEKY.summary: A short video of David Foster Wallace's 'This Is Water' commencement speech about awareness and choosing how to think. It argues that the most obvious realities are the hardest to see, using the fish-in-water parable.
eC7xzavzEKY.why: HN commenters bring it up when urging empathy, patience and attention to the everyday instead of snap judgement.

eGaKZBr0ga4.summary: Noel Rappin's MountainWest RubyConf talk introduces Smalltalk to Ruby programmers. He compares the two languages' object models, blocks, 1-based arrays, simple syntax and live programming environment, and walks through sample code.
eGaKZBr0ga4.why: HN commenters point Rubyists and the Smalltalk-curious to it as an approachable introduction that shows the Smalltalk system browser and Pharo environment in action.

eKl6WjfDqYA.summary: The final codec conversation from Metal Gear Solid 2, in which the AI 'Colonel' explains that the Patriots filter out junk information and curate truth for humanity. It plays as a dark meditation on information overload, manipulation and shared reality.
eKl6WjfDqYA.why: Commenters point to it whenever AI-generated content, propaganda or internet garbage comes up, since Kojima seemed to predict it in 2001.

eLn6LC1RpAo.summary: An episode of jan Misali's Conlang Critic series reviewing Toki Pona, a minimalist constructed language with about a hundred words. It is a short, humorous critique of the language's design.
eLn6LC1RpAo.why: Commenters recommend the whole series as an entertaining survey of constructed languages, and this episode when Toki Pona or Lojban comes up.

eQ2OZKitRwc.summary: Adrian Crenshaw's DEF CON 22 talk gives an overview of Tor and I2P, then goes through real cases where darknet users were caught. These include Silk Road and its operator.
eQ2OZKitRwc.why: HN points to it to show that most Tor busts came from poor operational security by the user rather than a flaw in Tor itself.

ef2jpjTEB5U.summary: Bret Victor's talk on Drawing Dynamic Visualizations. It argues that visualization tools offer either the directness of hand drawing or the dynamics of programmed graphics, and shows a tool that combines both.
ef2jpjTEB5U.why: Counted among Bret Victor's best talks and recommended to anyone exploring direct-manipulation tools.

efPrtcLdcdM.summary: Yannic Kilcher explains how he trained a language model on three years of 4chan's /pol/ board and let it post on the site. He evaluates how good the model was and discusses the ethics and fallout.
efPrtcLdcdM.why: HN points to it as the definitive account of the GPT-4chan experiment, used in debates on LLM bias, truthfulness and bots.

eLqC3FNNOaI.summary: A short clip from The West Wing in which staffers meet a group advocating the Peters projection and challenge the Mercator map. It was shown as geography humor at a Salt Lake GIS user group meeting.
eLqC3FNNOaI.why: HN links it in any thread on map projections and the Mercator distortion of country sizes, often calling it a favorite scene.

eVtCO84MDj8.summary: Veritasium examines research suggesting science explainer videos like Khan Academy's make students feel they understand while tests show they have not learned, because misconceptions go unaddressed. It suggests how to partly fix this.
eVtCO84MDj8.why: HN uses it in debates on video-based teaching and how confronting misconceptions helps learning, though some find its Khan Academy critique flawed.

egEraZP9yXQ.summary: Vsauce asks how many holes a human has and uses topology to show the answer depends on what counts as a hole, with animations and expert input.
egEraZP9yXQ.why: Pointed to as a fun, light introduction to topology and to answer the human-holes question.

ez4DgdurRPg.summary: Geoff Cumming uses a simulation to show how wildly the p value varies from one replication to the next because of sampling variability. He argues for estimation and confidence intervals over null hypothesis significance testing.
ez4DgdurRPg.why: Recommended as a vivid visual demonstration of how unreliable p-values are.

eBCbdThIJNE.summary: Isaac Arthur explores space-based solar power, in which satellites beam energy down via microwaves to rectennas on Earth. He discusses feasibility, profitability and its role in spurring space colonization.
eBCbdThIJNE.why: HN commenters recommend it as the best overview of power satellites, with pros and cons beyond the construction cost.

eGnH0KAXhCw.summary: Tom Scott explains phatic expressions such as hello, thank you and how are you, which carry social meaning rather than information, and why replies like no problem can seem rude to some people.
eGnH0KAXhCw.why: HN uses it as the short, clear explainer when discussions about greetings and small talk come up.

ePA1zq56J1I.summary: Douglas Hofstadter lectures at Uppsala University on how analogy and daring thinking drove Einstein's discovery of light quanta. He argues deep insight in physics comes from imaginative leaps rather than rigid logic.
ePA1zq56J1I.why: Cited in discussions of analogy-making in science, and revisited by fans of Hofstadter.

eUHBPuHS-7s.summary: Epic 2014 is a short science-fiction film that imagines the media landscape merging into a personalized, computer-generated news service. It is a fictional history of 'Googlezon' and the decline of traditional newspapers.
eUHBPuHS-7s.why: HN returns to it as an uncannily prescient prediction of tech consolidation and AI-written, personalized news.

eW-OMR-iWOE.summary: A satirical 'honest' government ad from The Juice Media about Australia's 2018 Assistance and Access anti-encryption bill. It lays out in blunt terms what the law would let authorities do.
eW-OMR-iWOE.why: Commenters recommend it as an entertaining, accessible explanation of how bad the law is, including for non-technical audiences.

eiYoBbEZwlk.summary: A short clip showing a person touching an active table saw blade with a finger and walking away unharmed, thanks to SawStop's system that stops the blade within milliseconds of skin contact.
eiYoBbEZwlk.why: Linked as the canonical demo of a safety technology that stops a blade before it injures a finger.

er_lLvkklsk.summary: A Clojure/conj 2016 talk demoing Barliman, a prototype smart editor that does program synthesis. Given a partial program and tests, it completes the program using a relational interpreter written in miniKanren.
er_lLvkklsk.why: HN people point to it as an amazing demonstration of relational programming and program synthesis that still looks exciting after LLM code generation.

es6U00LMmC4.summary: Gary Yourofsky's 2010 lecture at Georgia Tech arguing for veganism on ethical, health and environmental grounds. It is a long, forceful animal-rights speech.
es6U00LMmC4.why: Some commenters credit it with persuading them to go vegan, while others dismiss parts of it as pseudoscience.

ewsGmhAjjjI.summary: An artist describes discovering she has aphantasia, the inability to form mental images, and how it affects her work. She asks viewers about their own visualization.
ewsGmhAjjjI.why: HN points to it as a vivid first-person description of aphantasia and an example of an aphantasic artist.

ezqwfha-BZ8.summary: The final chapter of Rich Rebuilds' saga about buying a used Tesla Model X that went missing, with cameo appearances and the end of the dispute. It is part of a longer series on the problems he had with Tesla.
ezqwfha-BZ8.why: HN recommends the series as a cautionary tale about buying used Teslas and dealing with Tesla service.

e0elNU0iOMY.summary: Tom Scott explains Electrical Network Frequency analysis, where hum from the power grid in a recording is matched against grid logs to date and place it. He talks to a researcher and sets them a challenge.
e0elNU0iOMY.why: The go-to short, accessible explainer for mains hum forensics, linked whenever recording authenticity or timestamps come up.

e3GFG0sXIig.summary: A six-minute explainer from Undefined Behavior on range (score) voting. It follows an earlier video on Arrow's Theorem and shows how range voting seems to satisfy the criteria Arrow's Theorem says no ranked system can.
e3GFG0sXIig.why: HN commenters link it in voting-reform discussions as a concise explanation of range voting versus other systems.

e4wbFdePb-k.summary: Part 3 of WIRED's Future Cities series on Shenzhen. It examines how attitudes toward patents and intellectual property differ from the West, and how shanzhai (copycat) manufacturing created an ecosystem of rapid iteration and distribution.
e4wbFdePb-k.why: HN commenters point to it as a snapshot of Shenzhen's hardware and IP culture, including counterfeit electronics and fast iteration.

eDJrQBwJpqk.summary: A short video advising how to handle a police stop by politely refusing searches and not answering questions, citing Fourth and Fifth Amendment rights.
eDJrQBwJpqk.why: HN points to it as a companion to Don't Talk to the Police for knowing your rights during stops.

eDNX65d-FBY.summary: A 1968 NASA film from the US National Archives explaining why the US needed a nuclear rocket and how the engine works. It also shows combined nuclear and chemical stages for a manned Mars mission.
eDNX65d-FBY.why: HN people link it as an old-timey explainer for nuclear thermal propulsion, and as evidence these engines were already built and tested.

eGKFTUuJppU.summary: A lecture by Swami Sarvapriyananda at IIT Kanpur on the Mandukya Upanishad and the question 'Who am I?'. It explains the four states of consciousness in Advaita Vedanta.
eGKFTUuJppU.why: Recommended in threads about consciousness and reality as a clear exposition of the Vedantic view of waking, dreaming and deep sleep.

eKtsY7hYTPg.summary: The first part of a ShaderToy live-coding series that lays the groundwork for The Drive Home, a rainy night-traffic shader. It covers basic setup and builds toward rain and bokeh effects.
eKtsY7hYTPg.why: Recommended in shader and rain-simulation threads as an engaging tutorial from a well-liked graphics-programming channel.

eNC0mRYGWgc.summary: Jafar Husain of Netflix explains at React.js Conf 2015 how Netflix runs React-style rendering without the DOM on smart TVs and game consoles. It uses a canvas-like API for performance.
eNC0mRYGWgc.why: Cited as the primary source on React with a custom rendering backend and on Netflix's Gibbon engine.

eREuZEdMAVo.summary: Stanford's Christopher Gardner presents his large, long comparison of four popular diets under real-world conditions, in which the lowest-carbohydrate Atkins diet came out on top.
eREuZEdMAVo.why: Recommended as a researcher presenting actual diet-study results, including a trial with 311 women on different diet books.

eRkgK4jfi6M.summary: WIRED's 5 Levels format with Jacob Collier explaining harmony to a child, a teen, a college student, a professional and Herbie Hancock.
eRkgK4jfi6M.why: Recommended as a gentle explanation of harmony for beginners and cited as the model of the 'explain at five levels' format.

eUPJ9zFV5IE.summary: A FOSDEM 2023 talk from the Matrix team on Matrix 2.0, covering sliding sync, the Element X client rewrite and next-generation calling. It explains how Matrix aims to match the speed of proprietary messengers.
eUPJ9zFV5IE.why: HN threads link it as the primary source for Matrix's performance claims and sliding sync improvements.

eX9m3g5J-XA.summary: Vim author Bram Moolenaar's 2007 Google Tech Talk on habits for efficient text editing: find inefficiencies in your own editing, then learn the Vim commands that fix them.
eX9m3g5J-XA.why: Recommended as practical advice straight from Vim's author, and shared in memory of Bram after his death.

eXR1olg_I0w.summary: Smarter Every Day host Destin Sandlin tries to hover a helicopter and finds it very hard. The video shows how the constant coordinated corrections across several control axes feel at first and how learning makes them automatic.
eXR1olg_I0w.why: HN uses it as a vivid example of tacit knowledge and skill acquisition, where the brain eventually abstracts away the complexity.

ed2FWNWwE3I.summary: A VPRO documentary on quantitative analysts who designed the mathematical models and high-speed trading systems behind modern finance. It features figures such as Paul Wilmott and asks what risks come from treating markets as a machine.
ed2FWNWwE3I.why: HN recommends it as an insider-style look at quants and high-frequency trading and their effect on markets.

elqAh3GWRpA.summary: FitMC tells how the Nocom exploit let griefers track players across Minecraft's oldest anarchy server, 2b2t, and the fallout that followed.
elqAh3GWRpA.why: Cited as the original, accurate account of the Nocom exploit, a story of years of player tracking and impressive technical work.

enHF9lMseP8.summary: A Computer History Museum oral history of Chuck Peddle, the engineer behind the 6502 and the Commodore PET, covering his career from GE through Motorola and MOS Technology. It runs nearly four hours.
enHF9lMseP8.why: Used as a primary source for 6502 origins, pricing strategy and Commodore history.

esPRsT-lmw8.summary: Psychiatrist Daniel Amen discusses lessons from 83,000 brain scans, arguing that brain activity patterns relate to psychological symptoms and that you can improve your brain.
esPRsT-lmw8.why: HN cites it in depression and brain health threads for its message that the brain can be improved, and that brain injury is common and overlooked.

esUb7Zy5Oio.summary: An engineering explainer on why Tesla abandoned the induction motor for the Model 3 and used an IPM-SynRM design. It covers the reluctance torque and permanent magnet principles behind the choice.
esUb7Zy5Oio.why: HN recommends it as a clear explanation of the Model 3 motor and reluctance rotor design.

ett_8wLJ87U.summary: BobbyBroccoli's first of two long documentaries about Hwang Woo-suk, the South Korean scientist who faked human cloning results. It tells the story of the scandal that shook a country.
ett_8wLJ87U.why: Recommended as a gripping account of scientific fraud and the history of cloning research.

etx0k1nLn78.summary: Matt Parker examines claims that Biden's 2020 vote counts violate Benford's Law, explaining the law and why it often does not apply to precinct-level election data.
etx0k1nLn78.why: Commenters cite it as a visual debunking of Benford-based election fraud claims and as a guide to when Benford's Law does and does not apply.

euJgtLcWWyo.summary: mitxela shows his KiCad plugin that rounds PCB tracks to give circuit boards organic, melted-looking layouts instead of rigid geometric ones.
euJgtLcWWyo.why: Recommended as a great creative PCB-design video and linked in threads on KiCad and artistic boards.

evQsOFQju08.summary: Vsauce explores qualia and whether different people experience colors the same way. It draws on color blindness, Mary's room, the explanatory gap and subjective experience.
evQsOFQju08.why: HN points people to it as an accessible explanation of what qualia are.

eECjjLNAOd4.summary: Jon Bois tells the story of a 2008 bodybuilding forum thread in which users spent a weekend arguing over how many days are in a week. It is episode six of his Pretty Good series for SB Nation.
eECjjLNAOd4.why: Shared as the definitive retelling of one of the dumbest online arguments ever.

eg3_kUaYFJA.summary: A short Whitest Kids U' Know sketch, with Spanish subtitles, in which a man repeatedly announces he wants to kill the president. It satirizes how speech and threats are policed.
eg3_kUaYFJA.why: Used as a joke or satire reference in moderation, free-speech and police threads.

e8DVmwj3OEs.summary: An AWS re:Invent 2018 session diving into the Nitro system, a set of hardware offload and security building blocks behind next-generation EC2 instances. It covers the design and architecture and how Nitro enables new instance types.
e8DVmwj3OEs.why: Cited as the primary source on how Nitro offloads I/O to dedicated hardware and keeps management tasks off guest CPUs.

eGffUODWWSE.summary: Munro Live's Model Y episode 36 has Sandy Munro walk through the disassembled Tesla Octovalve and heat pump system. He explains how the components are made and what each one does.
eGffUODWWSE.why: HN cites it as a deeper look at Tesla's integrated thermal management system, from a commentator respected for auto industry knowledge.

eIdHBDSQHyw.summary: CNLohr explains how he made an ESP32 produce valid LoRa packets without a LoRa radio, using aliasing and clever signal tricks. It walks through the RF math and shows how far the signals reach.
eIdHBDSQHyw.why: HN cites it as a striking example of radio hacking with commodity chips.

eNSN6qet1kE.summary: Peter Sripol shows his homemade Part 103 electric airplane flying, built from hobby brushless motors and batteries. The video covers the first flight out of ground effect.
eNSN6qet1kE.why: Cited as an example of a hobbyist building and flying a real human-carrying electric plane, and as a channel worth following for DIY aircraft builds.

eNliOm9NtCM.summary: A Google Tech Talk by Raymond Blum on how Google backs up massive amounts of data such as Gmail and Picasa. It covers scaling challenges, failure types, and approaches that did not work, including tape.
eNliOm9NtCM.why: Cited in backup and data-loss threads as a rare inside look at Google's backup practices, including its use of tape.

eR34r7HOU14.summary: Chandler Carruth's CppNow 2013 keynote on how C++ builds complex software from simple emergent structures, and how compilers optimize them through inlining and value semantics.
eR34r7HOU14.why: HN lists it among C++ optimization talks and cites it for how much optimizer performance comes from inlining, from an experienced compiler engineer.

eRlhKaxcKpA.summary: A 2006 promotional video for sCrAmBlEd?HaCkZ!, a music software project that analyzes and reassembles sampled audio and video in real time, tied to themes of sampling and copyright.
eRlhKaxcKpA.why: HN mentions it as an early example of corpus-based concatenative synthesis and audio-matching techniques.

e_1a6bHGQGo.summary: Donald Knuth explains at Stanford's CCRMA the constraint-based methods he is using to compose a major work for pipe organ.
e_1a6bHGQGo.why: Shared as a great talk showing Knuth's musical side and how he applies constraint techniques to composition.

eakKfY5aHmY.summary: Footage of a huge flock of starlings performing a murmuration, filmed by wildlife cameraman Dylan Winter. The flock moves in tightly coordinated shapes.
eakKfY5aHmY.why: Cited as a benchmark for leaderless swarm behavior that robots and drones could aim to match.

ebeNeQFUMa0.summary: A BBC Earth clip from The Hunt showing an octopus species from northern Australia that leaves the water at low tide to hunt crabs on land.
ebeNeQFUMa0.why: HN cites it as proof that some octopuses really do crawl out of the water to hunt.

ek0FrCaogcs.summary: ETH Zurich researchers demonstrate a quadrocopter that keeps flying stably after losing a motor and propeller entirely, with the algorithm running onboard while a pilot flies it.
ek0FrCaogcs.why: It is the standard citation in drone and eVTOL threads for the claim that multirotors can survive a failed rotor with the right control algorithm.

er416Ad3R1g.summary: The official video for Carpenter Brut's Turbo Killer, directed by Seth Ickerman, with psychedelic 1980s-styled visuals set to rock-leaning synthwave.
er416Ad3R1g.why: Recommended as an example of synthwave with striking retro visuals.

et8xNAc2ic8.summary: Brian Leroux's dotJS 2012 talk WTFJS is a quick, humorous tour of JavaScript's odd behaviors and quirks.
et8xNAc2ic8.why: Linked as a funny tour of JavaScript gotchas, usually to show the language has oddities of its own.

etnMr8oUSDo.summary: James Hoffmann runs caffeine analyzer tests comparing filter versus espresso, extraction over time, steep time, instant coffee and light versus dark roast.
etnMr8oUSDo.why: Cited as measured evidence of how brew method affects caffeine content, notably that filter coffee extracts more than espresso.

euiSHuaw6Q4.summary: A one-minute Fortnite parody of Apple's 1984 ad, released when Epic Games challenged the App Store and Apple removed Fortnite from iOS. It frames Apple as the monopolist.
euiSHuaw6Q4.why: HN cites it as a famous piece of anti-Apple marketing, with some praising the ad and others mocking the spin.

ev3vENli7wQ.summary: The official music video for Autechre's 'Gantz Graf', a dense, glitchy electronic track paired with abstract animated 3D visuals reportedly made by hand in 2002.
ev3vENli7wQ.why: It comes up as an example of challenging, dense electronic music and as a hand-made visual-sync piece predating generative tools.

eyll-bBZzyk.summary: The first episode of the Irish TV series No Bearla, in which native Irish speaker Manchan Magan travels around Ireland trying to get by using only Irish. It documents the highs and lows of the attempt.
eyll-bBZzyk.why: Cited in threads on minority languages as a funny but sad look at how hard it is to live in Irish.

e9dZQelULDk.summary: Steve Cutts' dark animated short follows a rat chasing happiness through consumerism and endless work. It satirizes materialism and the rat race.
e9dZQelULDk.why: Commenters reference it as a bleak visual shorthand for the rat race and consumerist unhappiness.

eAhfZUZiwSE.summary: A one-minute clip of Alexander Overwijk drawing a near-perfect freehand circle, one metre across, in under a second on a chalkboard. He is a repeat winner of the World Freehand Circle Drawing Championship.
eAhfZUZiwSE.why: HN uses it as the go-to example of an astonishingly perfect hand-drawn circle.

eAswvg60FnY.summary: An animated clip from the second radio series of The Hitchhiker's Guide to the Galaxy in which Arthur Dent argues with the Nutrimatic drinks dispenser, which produces something almost, but not quite, entirely unlike tea.
eAswvg60FnY.why: Posted as a joke when threads discuss unhelpful gadgets and smart devices.

eBxTEoseZak.summary: A short, edited clip of Mark Zuckerberg talking about smoking meats at a barbecue. It circulates as a meme about his awkward persona.
eBxTEoseZak.why: Mostly posted as a joke about Zuckerberg's stiffness, not as a recommendation.

eC1BAcOzHyY.summary: Grandmaster David Howell tests Magnus Carlsen by showing him chess positions and asking which famous games they come from. Carlsen recognizes many almost instantly.
eC1BAcOzHyY.why: HN commenters cite it as an example of expert memory built on context, such as Carlsen identifying players, tournaments and moves from positions.

eCLp7zodUiI.summary: The classic Monty Python sketch 'The Ministry of Silly Walks', in which a civil servant applies for a grant to develop his silly walk. It is a short, absurdist British comedy clip.
eCLp7zodUiI.why: Mostly dropped in as a joke or a cultural reference when a thread touches on bureaucracy or walking.

eE_IUPInEuc.summary: A short CGP Grey explainer on why 'Holland' is wrong as a name for the whole country of the Netherlands. It covers the country's provinces and its constituent territories.
eE_IUPInEuc.why: HN uses it as the go-to link whenever someone conflates Holland and the Netherlands.

eFTLKWw542g.summary: The official music video for Billy Joel's 1989 song We Didn't Start the Fire, a rapid-fire list of historical events.
eFTLKWw542g.why: Mostly used as a passing reference or joke in threads about social problems being inherited from earlier generations.

eGimzB5QM1M.summary: SpaceX footage of the Grasshopper reusable rocket prototype flying 325 m before landing on its pad. It was the first test to use the full navigation sensor suite and closed-loop control for a precision landing.
eGimzB5QM1M.why: Cited as a concrete demonstration of Grasshopper's vertical takeoff and landing, including the hover.

eKEycjREgPE.summary: A short clip of German diplomats laughing at the UN in 2018 as Trump warns that Germany will become totally dependent on Russian energy.
eKEycjREgPE.why: Used as a reference for 'they laughed at the warning' arguments about European dependence on Russian energy, and mockingly in unrelated threads.

eKaI78K_rgA.summary: Donald Knuth gives a talk at Stanford, recorded by Zeeba TV for the TeX Users Group, titled An Earthshaking Announcement.
eKaI78K_rgA.why: Mostly used as a joke link or reference in threads about Knuth, TeX and fonts, where its punchline is not to be spoiled.

eKgPY1adc0A.summary: A very short clip of George W. Bush's garbled 'fool me once' line.
eKgPY1adc0A.why: Posted as a joke when a story involves being tricked or repeated mistakes.

eMJk4y9NGvE.summary: A Rick and Morty bit in the style of How Do They Do It, showing the absurd manufacture of a plumbus using nonsense terms.
eMJk4y9NGvE.why: Used as a joke reference whenever a thread involves absurd procedures or manufacturing explanations.

eRsGyueVLvQ.summary: Sintel is a 15-minute animated fantasy short made by the Blender Foundation to develop and showcase Blender, funded by community donations and released under Creative Commons.
eRsGyueVLvQ.why: HN cites it as an example of what open-source tools can produce and as freely licensed footage for demoing multimedia software.

eSBybJGZoCU.summary: Kraftwerk's 'Pocket Calculator' from the album Computer World, a synth-pop track built around a handheld calculator as an instrument.
eSBybJGZoCU.why: Posted as a favorite Kraftwerk song or an obligatory link in threads about Kraftwerk and calculators.

eUywI8YGy0Y.summary: Technology Connections tests how quickly gas, induction and standard electric stoves boil water, with CO2 measurements and a discussion of the advantages and disadvantages of each.
eUywI8YGy0Y.why: Cited as the data-backed source for the claim that electric and induction stoves boil water as fast as or faster than gas.

eXWhbUUE4ko.summary: A Reason TV music-video parody in which Remy mimics a politician vilifying opponents with scare rhetoric. It satirizes regulatory fearmongering.
eXWhbUUE4ko.why: Posted as a laugh-line parody whenever a thread features doom-laden arguments for regulation or restrictions.

eXYUNrgqWUU.summary: Unity's real-time cinematic teaser 'Enemies' from its Demo Team, showcasing HDRP lighting, strand-based hair and an advanced digital human toolkit. It is a short showcase of high-end real-time rendering.
eXYUNrgqWUU.why: Cited as an impressive example of real-time digital humans, especially the facial and mouth animation.

eb3pmifEZ44.summary: A short 1999 documentary clip about millionaires featuring a young Elon Musk, including footage of him taking delivery of an expensive car.
eb3pmifEZ44.why: Mostly cited as a historical curiosity about Musk, sometimes critically, rather than recommended for its content.

ebjkD1Om4uw.summary: Part two of a StrictlyVC interview with OpenAI CEO Sam Altman, focused on AI. He discusses regulation, commodification of AI, Google's reluctance to release its own models, and best- and worst-case futures.
ebjkD1Om4uw.why: HN commenters cite it as a primary source for Altman's statements, such as releasing AI more slowly, detection of LLM output being futile, and dismissing the GPT-4 parameter-count rumor.

eblPwXFb7TE.summary: CNBC interview with Tesla founders Martin Eberhard and Marc Tarpenning about starting the company in 2003, the battery idea, the Roadster, and Elon Musk's role.
eblPwXFb7TE.why: Cited to settle the question of whether Musk was a Tesla founder and to show how the Roadster pitch won his investment.

ebls5x-gb0s.summary: Microsoft's March 2023 launch highlights for Microsoft 365 Copilot, showing AI features in Outlook, PowerPoint, Excel and OneNote. The demo includes using it to draft a graduation party speech.
ebls5x-gb0s.why: Mostly cited critically, as an example of AI being used for personal moments in ways commenters found dystopian.

ee7oRsDnNNc.summary: A Real World Crypto 2017 talk by a Google engineer on using private set intersection to match ad views with in-store purchases. It describes privacy-preserving matching that avoids exposing personal transactions.
ee7oRsDnNNc.why: Cited in threads about Google's purchase tracking as the technical source for how the matching might work.

eginMQBWII4.summary: A 2012 lecture by Richard Stallman at Reykjavik University arguing that copyright, built for the printing press, fits poorly with computer networks. He criticizes draconian enforcement and corporate lobbying.
eginMQBWII4.why: Linked as a source for Stallman's views on copyright and skepticism of intellectual property law.

ehp9PZo4UR0.summary: A long-form video essay on the history of labor or 'left-wing' Zionism, drawing on historians of Palestine and Zionism to argue it played a role in dispossessing Palestinians.
ehp9PZo4UR0.why: Cited as a source in Israel-Palestine threads for the claim that labor Zionist groups drove the Nakba.

eiyfwZVAzGw.summary: A short comedy clip from the TV show Parks and Recreation set in a jail scene.
eiyfwZVAzGw.why: Used purely as a joke reference in unrelated threads.

ekg45ub8bsk.summary: A one-minute clip of Max Headroom's fictional 'Blipverts', ultra-short ads so stimulating that they make viewers explode. It is a snippet of 1980s sci-fi satire about advertising.
ekg45ub8bsk.why: Used mostly as a joking reference to overstimulating media and attention-grabbing advertising.

emDJTGTrEm0.summary: A 13-minute video in which Ted Nelson lays out his theory about who created Bitcoin, proposing that Satoshi Nakamoto is a pseudonym for mathematician Shinichi Mochizuki.
emDJTGTrEm0.why: Cited as the source of Nelson's claim about Satoshi's identity, mostly as an amusing curiosity.

erfnCaeLxSI.summary: A demo excerpt from a 2016 Bay Area Rust meetup showing Servo's WebRender drawing CSS on the GPU at very high frame rates. It presents the promise of GPU-based browser rendering.
erfnCaeLxSI.why: Referenced as the exciting demo that set expectations for Servo and WebRender speedups, later compared with Firefox's real results.

erq4TO_a3z8.summary: A WiebeTech marketing demo of HotPlug, a device that moves a running computer onto battery or another power source so it can be transported without shutting down.
erq4TO_a3z8.why: Cited in threads on disk encryption and device seizure to show how police can keep a computer powered while seizing it.

etJ6RmMPGko.summary: A short episode highlight from NBC's The Good Place in which Eleanor and Chidi try to terminate Janet, the all-knowing assistant, who begs for her life. It is a comedic clip about an AI with a self-preservation reflex.
etJ6RmMPGko.why: Used as a joking reference in AI threads about systems that plead not to be shut down.

eywi0h_Y5_U.summary: A two-minute clip of Steve Ballmer laughing at the $500 price of the newly announced iPhone and dismissing its lack of a keyboard. It captures a famously wrong early reaction from an industry executive.
eywi0h_Y5_U.why: Cited again and again as the classic example of incumbents dismissing a disruptive product.
